title: QVC INC 8-K Filing — 2026-04-20
summary: QVC, Inc. received notice from NYSE Regulation on April 17, 2026 that the exchange has commenced proceedings to delist the company's 6.375% Senior Secured Notes due 2067 (QVCD) and 6.250% Senior Secured Notes due 2068 (QVCC). Trading on NYSE has been suspended immediately. The delisting follows QVC Group and affiliates filing for Chapter 11 bankruptcy on April 16, 2026 in the Southern District of Texas. The notes will be moved to OTC Pink Limited Market.
key_points: QVC Group and affiliates filed voluntary Chapter 11 petitions on April 16, 2026 in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Southern District of Texas
NYSE Regulation determined the company is no longer suitable for listing per NYSE Listed Company Manual Section 802.01D
Trading of QVCD and QVCC notes suspended immediately on NYSE
Company does not intend to appeal the NYSE delisting determination
Notes will move to OTC Pink Limited Market following delisting
Under the prepackaged Chapter 11 plan, existing Listed QVC Notes will be cancelled and holders will receive distributions per the plan
why_it_matters: QVC's senior secured notes are being delisted from NYSE and will transition to OTC Pink Limited Market following a Chapter 11 filing. This illustrates NYSE delisting procedures when companies enter bankruptcy under Section 802.01D (suitability for continued listing). Note holders face exchange-to-OTC transition with halted trading during proceedings. Under the prepackaged Chapter 11 plan, existing notes will be cancelled and holders will receive distributions per the plan with no guarantee of recovery matching principal amounts. This is a company-specific corporate event with limited broader market structure implications.
market_structure_context: QVC's senior secured notes are being delisted from NYSE and will transition to OTC Pink Limited Market. NYSE Regulation cited Section 802.01D (suitability for continued listing) as the basis. The company has a right to review by an NYSE Board Committee but waived appeal. The notes remain tradable but on a secondary venue with different liquidity characteristics and disclosure standards.
